defects.claim_says: Section 3(d) (President's FACA functions for the Committee performed by the Administrator of General Services) is operative on 2026-10-14; 'no held instrument amends it'; the continuation orders are 'continuation events, not amendments'.
defects.source_says: EO 13591 sec. 4 (signed 2011-11-23): 'Notwithstanding the provisions of any other Executive Order, the functions of the President under the Federal Advisory Committee Act that are applicable to the committees listed in sections 1 and 2 of this order shall be performed by the head of the department or agency designated after each committee', and the SLTPS Committee is listed with (National Archives and Records Administration). The same override recurs in sec. 2 of EO 13652, 13708, 13811, 13889, 14048, 14109 and EO 14354 (current through 2027-09-30). These held texts displace the GSA assignment in sec. 3(d) from 2011-11-23; the claim neither records this override as a later event on sec. 3(d) nor tests it as an earlier end (supersession), so the clause's state and current predicate are unsupported.

reasoning: Identity confirmed (EO 13549 of August 18, 2010, 75 FR 51609, Classified National Security Information Program for SLTPS Entities); all 156 quoted spans match the held bytes; the 61-clause inventory covers the operative text from section 1 to section 7 with no gaps, and the 6(b) merge is correct. Section 7's own-terms end on 2011-02-14 (180 days after 2010-08-18) is computed correctly and the quote is exact. The OFR disposition note lists only See and Continued by entries, with no Revoked or Superseded note, and the cruden search found no revoking instrument. Two defects require rejection. First, every continuation order from EO 13591 onward assigns the President's FACA functions for this Committee to NARA 'Notwithstanding the provisions of any other Executive Order'. That conflicts directly with section 3(d), which assigns those functions to the GSA Administrator. The claim calls the continuation orders mere continuations and says no held instrument affects 3(d), so the override is not addressed and the clause's operative state is unsupported. Second, four continuation events carry signing dates as effective dates although each order states an effective date of September 30. The remaining clauses look sound on the held evidence, but the claim must be corrected and reviewed again at its new hash.

reasoning: Identity confirmed (Executive Order 12985 of January 11, 1996, 61 FR 1209, Establishing the Armed Forces Service Medal; the OFR record matches). All 15 quoted spans match the held bytes. Five clauses cover sections 1 to 4 with no gaps. Later events were checked against the held texts. EO 13286 sec. 20 strikes 'the Secretary of Transportation' in section 2 only, and its sec. 92 makes it effective March 1, 2003, which matches the claim. Section 4 still names the Secretary of Transportation, and the claim correctly says no instrument amends it. EO 13154 sec. 2 (May 3, 2000, no separate effective date) and EO 13289 sec. 3 (March 12, 2003, no separate effective date) each begin 'Notwithstanding section 3 of Executive Order 12985' and keep Kosovo and terrorism-operation qualifiers qualified, with an in-lieu option. The claim records them as exceptions that are later events, not ends, which is a correct reading. The OFR note ('Amended by: EO 13286, February 28, 2003; See: EO 13154') is fully addressed. The cruden search found only these instruments plus statutes and regulations that cite the order for veterans' definitions (38 U.S.C. 4212, 41 CFR 60-300.2, 48 CFR 22.1301, 5 CFR 307), which recognize the medal and do not end it. The standing award rules have no completion event and no own-terms end, and savings are not engaged. The current predicate is the own text plus the bounded searches, disclosed honestly.
